name: Kraft Heinz Co
moat_justification: A handful of genuinely strong brands (Heinz above all, Philadelphia) sit inside a broad portfolio that has lost volume and share to private label for a decade; the $9.3B of 2025 goodwill/intangible impairments are the filer's own admission that much of the brand equity was worth less than carried. Pricing power survives only in select categories and is bought back with volume losses, and only 21% of revenue was gaining or holding share in 2025 (36% YTD 2026). Weak-to-narrow and eroding: 4/10, CAP 7.2 years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Cash-generative packaged-food giant with an eroding narrow moat (4/10) — the OE is real but growth is negative, so at $22.70 it just misses the 15% hurdle (14.6% weighted, IV@15% $22.06); clears 15% only below ~$22.
moat_for: Heinz and Philadelphia 'win-big' brands gaining/holding share across regions and categories
Global distribution scale and shelf presence built over decades
Demonstrated pricing in select categories (Q2 2026 price +1.3pp)
Cash-generative core — OCF positive every filed year, $4.62B TTM
moat_against: Private-label share up from ~11% to ~17% since 2019, eroding pricing power
Volume/mix declining (-2.6pp in Q2 2026; meats and spoonables weakest)
Repeated goodwill/intangible impairments ($9.3B in 2025) — brands failing carrying-value tests
Only 21% of revenue gaining/holding share in 2025 (36% YTD 2026, still a minority)
Low returns on capital; dividend frozen at $0.40 since the 2019 cut
